result:
At the edge of town, there is a vending machine that sells nothing anyone can name. Its buttons are blank, its glass is dark, and its coin slot accepts only ordinary coins. Still, people visit every evening, carrying small change and larger questions they would never ask aloud.

One woman pressed the top button after losing her brother. A paper cup appeared, warm with tea that smelled like their childhood kitchen. A boy received a map of the city with every safe place circled in blue. The mayor got a single, perfectly sharpened pencil.

Nobody understood the rules. Sometimes the machine returned a coin and offered nothing at all. Sometimes it delivered a brass key, a packet of seeds, or an envelope containing three words in unfamiliar handwriting. The town argued over whether these were answers, accidents, or invitations to pay closer attention.

Years passed. The paint peeled. Someone planted flowers around its base, and someone else left a little roof to keep the rain away. Travelers began arriving just to see it. Most left disappointed, because a machine that gives people what they need looks remarkably like one that gives them nonsense.

Then one winter night, the power went out across town. In the darkness, neighbors brought candles and blankets and gathered beside the silent machine. They shared stories until morning. When the lights returned, no one hurried home. For once, nobody thought to put a coin in. They had already received something they could finally recognize clearly together.
